vulnerabilities.description: dpkg-deb does not properly sanitize directory permissions when extracting a control member into a temporary directory, which can leave temporary files behind on cleanup and, under repeated execution on adversarial .deb packages, lead to disk quota exhaustion or disk full conditions.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not extract .deb packages at runtime.

ratings.justification: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path invokes dpkg-deb, so the vulnerable extraction path is never reached.

analysis.detail: The leftover temporary files need dpkg-deb to extract the control member of an attacker-supplied .deb archive. dpkg is used only by the package manager while the image is built; the container entrypoint and the liquibase launcher script never invoke dpkg or dpkg-deb, the Liquibase CLI is a Java process, and lpm is a statically linked Go binary, so dpkg-deb's extraction path is never reached by Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu dpkg 1.21.1ubuntu2.6 (jammy) and 1.22.6ubuntu6.5 (noble); only Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 shipped an affected build (1.21.1ubuntu2.3), Liquibase Secure 5.0.1 ships 1.21.1ubuntu2.6, and Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 and later ship 1.22.6ubuntu6.5 or newer.
